{"id": "836d0e33-b7c7-491a-a869-024cda50721f", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_vSQxhyI6xCtY3kGhhJ8bsy", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot Windows patch installation failures in Systems Manager?\",\"context\":\"### Resolve system file corruption on your instance\\n\\nCorrupt systems files prevent Windows Update patch installations, even when network connectivity and Group Policy settings are correct. If you have corrupt system files that cause your Windows patch installation failures, then you might receive the following errors:\\n\\n* Patching operations fail when Run Command runs successfully.\\n* Component-Based Servicing (CBS) logs show Component Servicing Infrastructure (CSI) Payload Corruption errors.\\n* The **RestoreHealth** command in the Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM) repair tool fails. For more information, see [Use the System File Checker tool to repair missing or corrupted system files](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/use-the-system-file-checker-tool-to-repair-missing-or-corrupted-system-files-79aa86cb-ca52-166a-92a3-966e85d4094e) on the Microsoft website.\\n* Individual KB updates fail and return \\\"-2145124475\\\" or \\\"0x800f0985\\\" error messages.\\n\\nTo check for corrupted system files, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Review your CBS logs at %systemroot%\\\\\\\\Logs\\\\\\\\CBS.\\n2. In your logs, look for **CSI Payload Corrupt** entries.\\n3. Run the System File Checker command to identify and repair corrupt system files: \\n ```plaintext\\n sfc /scannow\\n ```\\n **Note:** If the System File Checker command doesn't repair the corrupt system files that it finds, then rerun the command. If the command can't repair your system files after three tries, then proceed to the next step.\\n4. Run the following **CheckHealth** command to check the Component Store of the Windows image for corrupt files: \\n ```plaintext\\n DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth\\n ```\\n **Note:** For information, see [/Cleanup-Image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/dism-operating-system-package-servicing-command-line-options?view=windows-11#cleanup-image) on the Microsoft website.\\n5. If the **CheckHealth** command detects corruption, then run the following **ScanHealth** command to check that the image is repairable: \\n `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth` \\n If the image is repairable, run the following **RestoreHealth** command: \\n `DISM /Online /Cleanup\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/systems-manager-patch-install-fail\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How can I restore a corrupt registry on my EC2 Windows instance?\",\"context\":\"Short description\\n------------------\\n\\nA corrupt Windows registry can cause an EC2 Windows instance to freeze, slow down, restart randomly, or become unusable.\\n\\nEven without performing other backup utilities or configurations beforehand, Windows regularly and automatically makes its own backup of the registry in the following location: \\n\\n```plaintext\\nC:\\\\Windows\\\\System32\\\\config\\\\RegBack\\n```\\n\\nEC2Rescue can restore these previously created backups from the RegBack directory to the current registry of the EC2 instance.\\n\\n Resolution\\n-----------\\n\\nTo use EC2Rescue to restore to the latest registry backup, follow these steps:\\n\\n1. **Warning**: If this instance has an [instance store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html) volume, you'll lose any data on it when the instance is stopped. Be sure to back up the contents of the volume before stopping it. \\n[Stop the inaccessible instance](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/Stop_Start.html#starting-stopping-instances). \\n**Note**: If you aren't using an [Elastic IP Address](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/elastic-ip-addresses-eip.html), the public IP address will be released when you stop the instance.\\n2. [Create an EBS-backed Amazon Machine Image](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/Creating_EBSbacked_WinAMI.html) (AMI). From the [Amazon EC2 console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/ec2/), select your instance. For **Actions**, choose **Image**, **Create Image**.\\n3. [Launch a new instance](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/launching-instance.html) (Windows Server 2012 or later) in the same AWS Region and Availability Zone as the inaccessible instance. You will use this new instance as the recovery instance. \\n**Note**: You can terminate the recovery instance after the corrupted registry is restored.\\n4. [Detach the boot volume](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/ebs-detaching-volume.html) of the corrupt instance.\\n5. [Attach the volume](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/ebs-attaching-volume.html) to the recovery instance as a secondary volume using the default settings in the Amazon EC2\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/restore-corrupt-registry-windows\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot status check failures on my Amazon EC2 Windows instance?\",\"context\":\"### Troubleshoot an OS that fails to boot\\n\\nTroubleshoot issues with your EC2 instance [based on the screenshot that you receive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ics-common.html). If you see the blue screen (0xc000000e), then see [Disk signature collision](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/win-ts-common-issues.html#disk-signature-collision).\\n\\nIf you receive a \\\"Stuck Windows Update (error C0000034)\\\" error, then complete the following steps to troubleshoot:\\n\\n1. [Launch a rescue instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/LaunchingAndUsingInstances.html).\\n2. [Stop the original instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Stop_Start.html#stop-instance-with-graceful-os-shutdown).\\n3. [Detach the root volume from the original instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-detaching-volume.html#detach).\\n4. [Attach the volume to the rescue instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-attaching-volume.html).\\n5. Run the following command on the rescue instance to remove pending actions:\\n ```plaintext\\n DISM /image:D:\\\\ /cleanup-image /revertpendingactions\\n ```\\n **Note:** Replace **D:** with your volume's letter drive. \\n If you don't see the attached volume in the command's output, then verify that the volume is online. Run the following command to open **Disk Management**:\\n ```plaintext\\n diskmgmt.msc\\n ```\\n Then, open the context (right-click) menu for the volume, and then choose **Online**. Then, rerun the **cleanup-image** command.\\n6. [Unmount and detach the volume from the rescue instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-detaching-volume.html#umount-detach-volume).\\n7. [Attach the volume to the original instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-attaching-volume.html) as the **/dev/sda1** root volume.\\n8. [Start the original instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Stop_Start.html#start-ec2-instance).\\n\\nIf you see \\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-windows-status-check-failures\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up AWS/Microsoft guidance for fixing persistent DISM component store corruption."}
